title: 1993 Tehran mid-air collision
summary: Flight 962 was climbing after takeoff from Tehran Mehrabad to Mashhad when it collided with a Sukhoi Su-24 fighter jet. The Tu-154 was cleared to climb to 6000 ft while Su-24s were descending to land on a parallel runway. One Su-24 turned left without adequate visibility and collided with the climbing airliner. The Tu-154's rear engine and tail were torn off.
probable_cause: Air traffic controller allowed Flight 962 to climb while Su-24s were descending without proper separation. Controller failed to inform Flight 962 about the Su-24s in their airspace. Sukhoi pilots failed to maintain assigned altitude.

title: Palair Macedonian Airlines 301
summary: The Fokker 100 crashed shortly after takeoff in snowy conditions due to ice accumulation on the wings. The aircraft had been parked in snow and refueled; ice around the wing roots melted from fuel temperature but ice on the wingtips remained. The crew elected not to de-ice the aircraft and encountered control problems during takeoff that caused the crash.
probable_cause: Ice accumulation on the aircraft wings that was inadequately de-iced before takeoff. The crew conducted only a tactile check and opted not to use ground de-icing equipment.

factors.evidence: During the refueling, the ice around the wings' roots had melted due to the temperature of the fuel, while the ice on the tips hadn't.
The crew opted not to de-ice the aircraft, thinking that most of the ice had melted and the remaining was safe enough for flying.
A crew switch was conducted and a new set of pilots were brought in; the Macedonian co-pilot was undergoing training to transfer from Boeing 737 to Fokker 100.
The FSE performed a tactile check by rubbing his hand over the wings but did not request de-icing.
The aircraft eventually encountered control problems during takeoff, which caused it to crash.

events.text: The aircraft arrived in Skopje after a flight from Frankfurt, and was parked in Skopje in snowy conditions.
The aircraft was refueled with approximately 2,000 liters of fuel during which ice around the wings' roots had melted due to the temperature of the fuel.
A second refueling was commenced and the FSE performed a tactile check by rubbing his hand over the wings, but did not request de-icing.
The aircraft was cleared for take-off and eventually encountered control problems during takeoff, which caused it to crash.

title: Indian Airlines 491
summary: Flight 491 took off from Aurangabad with the captain's false perception of takeoff technique. The aircraft did not lift off until near the end of the 6000-foot runway. The left landing gear and left engine struck a truck carrying cotton bales at the runway end. This severed the landing gear and damaged control surfaces. The aircraft continued flight but impacted high-tension power lines 3 km from the airport and crashed.
probable_cause: The captain's false perception of takeoff technique resulted in a late rotation and impact with a truck at the runway end. The report blamed authorities for not regulating public vehicles near the airport's vicinity.

factors.evidence: The crash was caused by the captain's false perception on take-off technique

title: 1993 Zambia national football team plane crash

location.name: Atlantic Ocean, 500 m offshore from Libreville, Gabon

summary: A de Havilland Canada DHC-5 Buffalo transport aircraft of the Zambian Air Force carrying the Zambia national football team crashed into the Atlantic Ocean shortly after taking off from Libreville, Gabon, on April 27, 1993. All 25 passengers and five crew members were killed. The aircraft had previously experienced engine problems in Brazzaville but continued to Libreville where the left engine caught fire and failed. The pilot, who had also flown the team from Mauritius the previous day, mistakenly shut down the right engine in response, causing the aircraft to lose all power during climb and fall into the water 500 meters offshore.
probable_cause: The left engine caught on fire and failed. The pilot, suffering from fatigue, mistakenly shut down the right engine due to a faulty warning light instead of the burning left engine, causing loss of all power during climb-out. Prior to departure, maintenance checks had revealed defects in the engine including carbon particles in oil filters and disconnected cables.

factors.evidence: The pilot mistakenly shut down the right engine, causing the plane to lose all power during the climb out from Libreville Airport.
The left engine caught fire and failed a few minutes after taking off from Libreville.
A Gabonese report attributed the pilot's actions to fatigue after flying the team from Mauritius the previous day.
The plane lost all power during climb and fell into the water 500 m offshore.

events.text: Aircraft departed Brazzaville, Congo with Zambian football team aboard.
Aircraft arrived at Libreville, Gabon for refueling despite engine problems noted in Brazzaville.
A few minutes after taking off from Libreville, the left engine caught fire and failed.
Pilot mistakenly shut down the right engine in response to the left engine fire, causing the aircraft to lose all power and fall into the Atlantic Ocean 500 m offshore.

title: SAM Colombia 501
summary: SAM Colombia Flight 501 crashed into Mount Paramo Frontino during descent on approach to Medellín. Thunderstorm activity made ADF navigation difficult and the Medellín VOR/DME was unserviceable, causing the crew to descend before reaching the navigation beacon.
probable_cause: Navigation error due to unreliable ADF in thunderstorm conditions and unserviceable airport VOR/DME, with crew descending prematurely.

factors.evidence: Thunderstorm activity in the area made automatic direction finder navigation more difficult
aircraft had not yet reached the beacon and descended into mountainous terrain

events.text: Flight 501 took off from Panama City, Panama, bound for Bogotá, Colombia.
The aircraft climbed to flight level 160 as thunderstorm activity affected navigation.
The crew reported over the Abejorral NDB beacon at FL160.
The flight was then cleared to descend to FL120 after which communication was lost.
The flight then struck the 3,749 m Mount Paramo Frontino.

title: Merpati Nusantara Airlines 724
summary: Fokker F28 approached Jefman Airport in inclement weather with heavy rain and strong winds. Pilot descended extremely low (less than one metre), left landing gear struck small hill summit. Aircraft climbed but failed to recover, wing detached, entered spin and crashed into sea offshore.
probable_cause: Pilot disorientation due to inclement weather; crew mistakenly turned toward sea instead of runway; ATC warned to divert but pilot insisted on landing.

title: Asiana Airlines 733
summary: Flight 733 made three landing attempts at Mokpo Airport in heavy rain and wind. After two failed attempts, the aircraft impacted Mt. Ungeo at 800 ft altitude. Mokpo Airport was equipped only with VOR/DME navigation, with no precision approach capability.
probable_cause: Pilot error in flying below the minimum safe altitude of 1600 ft, descending to 800 ft, and continuing approach in poor visibility without required visual references.

title: 1993 Tajik Air Yakovlev Yak-40 incident
summary: A Yakovlev Yak-40 crashed during takeoff at Khorog Airport when militants forced the crew to accept 81 passengers on an aircraft designed to carry only 28, exceeding maximum takeoff weight by 3,000 kg. Unable to become airborne, the aircraft overran the runway at high speed. The left main landing gear struck an earth embankment 148-150 meters beyond the runway end. The aircraft then struck a boulder and a concrete pillbox before falling into the Panj River and disintegrating. Four passengers survived.
probable_cause: Severe aircraft overloading caused by forced acceptance of excess passengers under threat during civil war, preventing takeoff and causing runway overrun with terrain strike.

title: Avioimpex 110
summary: Flight 110 was an international scheduled passenger flight originating in Geneva, Switzerland with a final destination of Skopje, Macedonia. Due to a blizzard at Skopje, Flight 110 was diverted to Ohrid Airport. The Yak-42 was approximately 2,300 ft too high to carry out a successful landing, so a missed approach procedure was executed. Shortly afterwards the crew of Flight 110 radioed that they were not receiving the VOR signal. The aircraft crashed about 7 km east of Ohrid Airport.
probable_cause: The cause of the crash was attributed to a violation of the airport traffic pattern by the crew of Flight 110, who initiated a turn into rising terrain. A contributing factor was their decision to proceed with the approach even though they were not receiving a navigational signal.
